risks.note: Identified as a material risk in the BRSR: in pharmaceutical manufacturing, health and safety management systems must ensure uninterrupted and safe operations; incidents can have negative financial implications. Mitigated through systems aligned to the Factories Act, Explosives Act and ISO standards, with periodic audits and corrective/preventive action after incident reviews.
risks.risk: Occupational health and safety in chemical manufacturing

risks.note: The Company's operations, if not managed properly, may result in risk to the environment, with negative financial implications. Managed through established environment management practices, risk assessments, periodic reviews and ISO 14001 certification.

Manufacturing requires abundant quantities of raw materials and proper management of waste generated; waste management risks may result in negative financial implications. Mitigated via recycle-and-reuse programmes, solvent recovery and reuse, green chemistry, and handling of solid waste per MoEFCC and Pollution Control Board conditions.

Increased GHG emission levels may pose harmful effects to the environment and human health with negative financial implications. Mitigated by reducing dependency on fossil fuels, shifting to renewable sources for power and heat, SBTi-approved near-term and net-zero targets, and annual external verification of the GHG footprint per ISO 14064-1.
risks.risk: Climate change and greenhouse gas emissions

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as a material responsible-business-conduct risk (water footprint, consumption, intensity and discharge are BRSR-Core assured attributes); the detail of the disclosure is truncated in the routed text.

Global trade architecture is shifting from integrated globalisation toward fragmented networks driven by geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain disruptions and regulatory divergence, pushing procurement toward risk-adjusted frameworks, supplier diversification and inventory buffering. The Board notes FY 2025-26 was marked by a challenging global environment with evolving geopolitical and trade dynamics.
risks.risk: Geopolitical uncertainty, trade fragmentation and supply chain disruption

risks.note: Escalating expectations for GMP, batch-to-batch consistency, data integrity and environmental and safety norms are raising both capital and operating intensity; compliance credibility becomes a key differentiator influencing supplier selection and contract longevity.

Pricing and reimbursement pressures across developed markets are intensifying scrutiny on value delivery and utilisation, and growth is becoming highly selective, concentrating in therapies with differentiated clinical outcomes.
risks.risk: Pricing and reimbursement pressure in developed markets
